Combined deficiency of coagulation factors VIII and IX defines a blood coagulation disorder.

MHC-I immunodeficiency; chronic bronchitis and sinusitis in 3/3, bronchiectasis in 1/1. Recurrent GI infection alone does not establish lasting GI damage.

Benign tumor of Leydig cells, the hormone-producing endocrine cells of the gonad.
Inherited hair disorder with sparse scalp hair in 4/4 patients.
Congenital pits at the oral commissures affect the lips and oral structures; preauricular pits alone do not establish hearing damage.
Type I interferon-mediated autoinflammation; AGS-spectrum encephalopathy is the predominant RNASEH2A presentation, supporting neurologic damage in >30%.
Umbrella disorder of the nails; infection is only one subtype.
Psychiatric anxiety disorder; palpitations during panic attacks do not establish cardiovascular damage.
Chronic arachnoid inflammation; visual and hearing impairment each annotated 80-99%. Infectious or immune-mediated etiology is not universal.
Muscular dystrophy with defining ID/ataxia; cataract annotated 30-79%. Hepatic steatosis is 5-29%; transaminases may originate from muscle.
Combined lipid disorder and hearing impairment define the syndrome; corneal arcus is non-damaging and atherosclerosis is a separate disease.
Myoepithelial neoplastic proliferation confined to breast ducts; breast has no axis.
Reproductive inability to conceive; endocrine and other underlying causes are separate diagnoses and are not universal.
Defined by immunodeficiency in the PTEN syndrome spectrum; supplied evidence does not establish additional organ damage in at least 30%.
Malignant embryonal tumor originating in the cerebellum; myogenic differentiation does not indicate skeletal muscle involvement.
Neurotoxicity is defining; hypertension occurs in 30-79%. Anemia and renal tubular dysfunction are 5-29%; GI symptoms alone do not establish organ damage.
Developmental delay and intellectual disability define the syndrome; congenital heart defects occur in roughly 40-50%. Renal defects are not established at >=30%.
GM2 storage with progressive neurodegeneration; blindness and hearing impairment each 80-99%. Kyphosis also 80-99%, omitted under the four-axis cap.
Congenital cleft of the oral palate; associated maxillary hypoplasia affects facial bone development in 30-79%.
Active microbial infection of a peritesticular hydrocele; reproductive anatomy has no axis, and urinary involvement is not required.
Thyroid hormone overproduction defines the disease; systemic symptoms do not establish organ damage, and autoimmune etiology is not universal.
Congenital portosystemic venous shunt defined by diversion of portal blood away from the liver and reduced hepatic perfusion; encephalopathy is not universal.
